title: Top-down PLM assembly with temporal-scale transfer and distributed state ablation
question: Does a distributed bank of fixed exponential memory traces transfer history-conditioned decision capability to unseen temporal filter constants better than a compact three-timescale state, when the policy capacity is matched?
hypothesis: A temporally distributed state bank spanning a broader range of decay constants should represent unseen temporal filters more faithfully than a compact three-timescale bank, improving held-out history-conditioned exact decision capability without changing the visible current-observation interface or learned policy parameter count.

endpoints.name: heldout_temporal_success
endpoints.description: Exact class-balanced success on test histories generated from temporal filter constants that are not present in the training filter set; primary decision at H=256.

endpoints.name: interpolation_success
endpoints.description: Exact success on held-out temporal constants lying inside the training alpha range.

endpoints.name: extrapolation_success
endpoints.description: Exact success on held-out temporal constants slower than the largest training alpha.

endpoints.name: history_conditioned_action_gap
endpoints.description: Fraction of exact negation pairs with identical current observation but opposite correct actions for which the policy selects opposite actions.

endpoints.name: state_reset_shuffle
endpoints.description: Frozen-checkpoint reduction in distributed_eight performance after state reset or cross-episode state shuffle.

endpoints.name: computation_work
endpoints.description: Explicit evaluation work including state updates, state readout, router arithmetic and independent verification.

decision_rule.condition: At H=256, distributed_eight exceeds three_timescale in heldout_temporal_success by more than the preregistered materiality threshold 0.10, the registered seed-bootstrap 95% confidence interval for the paired seed-level difference excludes zero, and distributed_eight exceeds no_state.
decision_rule.licenses: bounded evidence that a broader distributed exponential memory bank improves temporal-filter transfer on the registered synthetic benchmark under matched learned-policy parameter count.
decision_rule.does_not_license: power-law or scale-free memory, biological equivalence, general temporal optimality, natural-language/vision/audio capability, asymptotic scaling, or hardware speedup.

decision_rule.condition: distributed_eight does not beat three_timescale materially, but the state arms retain a measurable history-conditioned action gap and outperform no_state.
decision_rule.licenses: persistent multi-timescale state is useful on the transfer benchmark, but broader scale coverage is not established as necessary.
decision_rule.does_not_license: three-timescale optimality or failure of distributed memory generally.

decision_rule.condition: distributed_eight fails to outperform no_state and three_timescale on the held-out transfer endpoint.
decision_rule.licenses: the registered distributed-timescale transfer hypothesis is not established on this benchmark.
decision_rule.does_not_license: failure of temporal memory generally, failure on other temporal distributions, or failure of PLM.

interpretation_order: representability of held-out temporal filters through the state map
held_constant: training and test temporal-filter constant sets are committed before confirmation and are disjoint
current observation at decision is exactly 0.0
paired test histories are exact negations with opposite gold actions
policy parameter count is 86 for no_state, two_timescale, three_timescale and distributed_eight; one_timescale is explicitly a lower-capacity 82-parameter control
optimizer family, learning rate, training step count and evaluation sample count
distributed_eight trace alphas are fixed before confirmation
